text:
sara_sales: Swimlane wants to migrate a POC from CompetitorX -> Redwood next Tue. Asks: pricing for ~10M tokens/mo, header-preserve proxy behavior, streaming chunk compatibility, JSON response parity, security questionnaire answers, IP/data residency. Can we run a quick preflight today to list blockers?

omar_solutions: I can own pricing + proxy behavior. Quick notes: our published per-token tiers cover this volume; recommend a POC promo (50% off month 1) to close. Streaming: CompetitorX emits small framed chunks; our stream is SSE-style with newlines. We can emulate their framing with a small translator shim (stream_delimiter flag) — will validate latency impact.

jin_eng: We can add header passthrough at the ingress translator. Need explicit allowlist from Swimlane though — we currently strip sensitive headers by default (e.g., cookie). If they require passthrough for auth headers we'll need legal signoff. Ask them for exact header list.

laura_cs: Pinged Swimlane for headers + an example request/response pair. Also requested their security questionnaire PDF. They want our answers by EOD Friday.

karthik_sece: Security summary: Data residency can be satisfied by provisioning Dedicated in us-east-1 or offering Private. For questionnaires we have the standard compliance pack (SOC2 + ISO snippets). If they request customer-managed KMS, we can support it on Private and with an enterprise contract. Any ask to persist full raw request bodies will need CISO approval.

omar_solutions: On response parity — biggest practical deltas are stop-sequence handling and whitespace trimming. CompetitorX treats stop tokens as message-level termination (strips trailing tokens) while we currently return the raw stream up to the stop. Example of their payload: ```json
{"prompt":"...","stop":["\n\n"]}
``` We can either (A) offer a compatibility flag that post-processes the response to match their semantics, or (B) advise client-side normalization. Jin, do we want route-level compat?

jin_eng: I can add a translator param: compat_stop_sequences=true. Quick nginx-ish patch for header allowlist I will test: ```nginx
# translator ingress snippet
proxy_set_header X-Allow-Preserve "x-client-id,x-forwarded-for,authorization";
``` Will run e2e in staging.

sara_sales: Thanks. Related billing question from Swimlane: they round tokens per 10-token buckets today — will that cause disputes? Also they asked about invoice/stamping for fintech audits (do we provide detailed per-request token logs?).

karthik_sece: Rounding per 10 tokens is acceptable. For regulated fintech, recommend Private deployment + dedicated audit log export — we can provide per-request tokenization logs under an NDA. I'll draft a Third-Party Risk Assessment response and mark the items needing legal/ciso approval.

laura_cs: Swimlane just uploaded their security doc + sample traffic (sensitive fields redacted). I put the files in our presales drive: https://redwood.app/drive/swimlane/presales — asked them for the header list and current tokenization settings.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: quick FYI — staging cluster rwd-staging-5 is free for smoke runs. Recommend running the translator patch and a streaming parity test (10 test prompts, 0.7 temp) after Jin's changes. :rocket:

jin_eng: Will run smoke and post results/logs here. If all green Omar, please send POC pricing proposal. ETA tomorrow noon. :+1:

sara_sales: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll wait for the smoke logs then finalize the POC SOW and get legal looped for KMS/data export notes. :thumbsup:
